locator: §2.6 Removal of duplicate rows, final sentence
claim: SQLite applies no type coercions during DISTINCT comparisons.
quote: BLOB affinity is used for DISTINCT comparisons, hence no type coercions occur.

claim: Without affinity conversion, a SQLite INTEGER or REAL compares below and therefore unequal to any TEXT value.
quote: An INTEGER or REAL value is less than any TEXT or BLOB value. When an INTEGER or REAL is compared to another INTEGER or REAL, a numerical comparison is performed.

claim: SQLite BLOB affinity preserves input storage classes without coercion.
quote: A column with affinity BLOB does not prefer one storage class over another and no attempt is made to coerce data from one storage class into another.

locator: §7.1 Assigning Collating Sequences from SQL, first paragraph
claim: SQLite columns default to BINARY collation unless another collation is explicitly defined.
quote: Every column of every table has an associated collating function. If no collating function is explicitly defined, then the collating function defaults to BINARY.

claim: SQLite ignores numeric arguments in parentheses following a declared type name.
quote: Note that numeric arguments in parentheses that following the type name (ex: "VARCHAR(255)") are ignored by SQLite

claim: SQLite INTEGER-affinity columns apply the same storage conversions as NUMERIC-affinity columns.
quote: A column that uses INTEGER affinity behaves the same as a column with NUMERIC affinity.
